stage3_evidence.source: the three kept run traces of the 2026-09-22 owner-authorised pilot (--keep-temp)
stage3_evidence.stability: byte-identical in all three runs; the only tool identifiers in any trace were Skill and Bash
stage3_evidence.mapping_command_invoked: type tool_used, tool Skill, input_match businessops:<command>, min 1
stage3_evidence.mapping_command_not_invoked: type tool_used, tool Skill, input_match businessops:<command>, min 0, max 0
stage3_evidence.why_min_zero_accompanies_max_zero: The platform evaluates a tool_used grader as min = e.min ?? 1, max = e.max ?? Infinity, and its verdict is count >= min && count <= max. With max 0 and no min the expected range is 1..0, which no count can satisfy, so the grader could never succeed. min 0 with max 0 is the only correct representation of an absence assertion.
stage3_evidence.limitation_skill_spelling: All 24 mappings are command invocations, which is what the pilot observed. No skill-only invocation was observed. The 22 routing skill_invoked and skill_not_invoked graders were mapped in Phase 1 to tool Skill with the bare skill name as input_match, which matches as a substring whether or not the runtime prefixes it; that mapping is unchanged and is not claimed to be proved by this pilot.
